themes_detail.label: Street Noise Surge
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints spiked to 42 THIS WEEK versus a baseline average of 9.6 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 336% increase (z-score: 5.59)—suggesting a possible localized disturbance, construction, or event-driven activity requiring urgent investigation.
evidence: 42 street/sidewalk noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 9.6 weekly average (336% spike, z-score: 5.59)
Vehicle noise complaints also up 189% THIS WEEK (13 complaints vs. 4.5 avg, z-score: 5.13)
Concurrent spike in two noise categories suggests event-driven or infrastructure activity
reporting_angles: Interview residents in high-complaint blocks; identify whether complaints cluster around specific locations or times of day
Check for active construction permits, street events, or nightlife venues licensed to operate in affected area

themes_detail.label: Graffiti Crisis Explodes
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints exploded to 26 LAST WEEK from a baseline of 1.2 per week over 8 weeks—a 1980% spike (z-score: 17.78, the highest severity signal in the dataset)—indicating either coordinated vandalism, gang activity, or widespread deterioration of public space.
evidence: 26 graffiti complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.2 weekly baseline (1980% increase, z-score: 17.78—highest severity signal)
Unprecedented spike suggests sudden onset rather than gradual decline
Correlated street/curb condition complaints (5 THIS WEEK vs. 1.0 avg) suggest broader infrastructure decay
reporting_angles: Visual documentation: photograph hotspot blocks and interview affected business owners; identify if tags are coordinated (gang markers, crew tags, or political statements)
NYPD briefing: request crime/gang intel for CD 317; ask Parks Dept about graffiti removal response times and resources

themes_detail.label: Vehicle Abandonment Wave
themes_detail.summary: Abandoned vehicle complaints jumped to 28 LAST WEEK from an 8-week baseline of 8.2 per week—a 239% spike (z-score: 5.29)—suggesting possible economic displacement, fleet dumping, or policing enforcement gaps.
evidence: 28 abandoned vehicle complaints LAST WEEK vs. 8.2 weekly average (239% increase, z-score: 5.29)
Sustained spike suggests ongoing source rather than one-time incident
Overlaps with broader street condition deterioration signal (graffiti, curb damage, dangling signs)
reporting_angles: File FOIL request for NYPD tow data and vehicle titles to identify whether vehicles are truly abandoned or belong to vulnerable populations
Interview Sanitation/DOT about removal capacity and backlog in CD 317

themes_detail.label: Sidewalk & Root Damage Spike
themes_detail.summary: Root, sewer, and sidewalk condition complaints rose to 5 THIS WEEK from a baseline of 1.8 per week—a 186% spike (z-score: 3.92)—alongside a 400% surge in curb condition complaints (5 LAST WEEK vs. 1.0 avg), signaling accelerating infrastructure failure.
evidence: 5 root/sewer/sidewalk complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.8 weekly baseline (186% increase, z-score: 3.92)
5 curb condition complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.0 baseline (400% increase, z-score: 4.62)
Convergence of two related infrastructure complaint types suggests systemic failure (tree root damage, subsurface settlement, or aging sewer mains)
reporting_angles: Request DEP and Parks Department inspection maps for CD 317; identify streets with most complaints and ask about planned repairs
Interview residents with trip hazards/damaged driveways; document photo evidence for liability angle

themes_detail.label: Dead Tree Epidemic
themes_detail.summary: Dead/dying tree complaints surged to 6 THREE WEEKS AGO from a baseline of 0.5 per week—a 1100% spike (z-score: 7.78)—indicating potential disease outbreak, pest infestation, or prolonged neglect of street tree stock.
evidence: 6 dead/dying tree complaints 3 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.5 weekly baseline (1100% increase, z-score: 7.78)
Spike is not this week but remains statistically extreme; timing suggests onset ~3 weeks prior
Correlates with broader infrastructure deterioration theme (graffiti, abandoned vehicles, sidewalk damage)
reporting_angles: Interview Parks Department arborist; request tree health assessments and disease/pest surveys for CD 317
Document which blocks are affected; determine if pattern follows water main breaks, soil contamination, or specific tree species
